rationale: SourceConfiguration::load reads book.src and preprocessor.dada.lean-source from the same book.toml used by Inventory::load and process_configured. check_context compares those fields with the runtime mdBook context before processing. Both root accessors route through input_path, whose normal-relative-path and canonical-containment checks reject outside-project paths, including symlink escapes. The production process_configured path passes the canonical project root separately from the Lean root to Rust selection; render_unit and Inventory::add_unit both select Rust citations relative to that project root. Inventory::inputs includes tool:book.toml, selects Lean targets using the configured Lean root, and enumerates conservative Lean source and Lake/toolchain context under that root. The cited configured_lean_root_is_shared_by_rendering_and_evidence test starts with current fixture reviews, changes to formal/model, observes stale evidence, verifies the replacement packet and rendered selection use the new value and path, rejects a conflicting runtime override, and renders Rust from the project root. I read the entire test and ran it in the passing evidence_validation binary. The original configured-root exploit in the frozen adversarial report is closed by shared selection plus configuration fingerprinting, rather than fingerprinting alone.
limitations: This contract concerns the production mdBook entry point process_configured; the lower-level process_with_lean helper intentionally accepts caller-supplied roots for fixtures and is not the configured boundary.

Canonical path containment is supported here by helper inspection. The cited configuration regression covers the nested Lean root and conflicting runtime root, not an exhaustive matrix of filesystem/configuration cases.
No claim is made that all renderer output or all legacy requirements have correspondence evidence.
